title: How to edit the master slide in Keynote on Mac: slide layouts, step by step

description: How to edit the master slide in Keynote on Mac: open View, choose Edit Slide Layouts, then rename, add placeholders and change any layout.

intro: To edit the master slide in Keynote on Mac, click the View menu button in the toolbar and choose Edit Slide Layouts, or press Shift-Command-E. Apple now calls the master a slide layout, so that is the name you will see in the slide navigator and the menus.
tldr: Apple now calls the master slide a slide layout in Keynote on Mac.
Click View in the toolbar, then Edit Slide Layouts. Shift-Command-E does the same.
Select a layout in the slide navigator to rename it, add placeholders or change its objects.
Click Done in the blue bar to leave. Changes reach every slide built on that layout.

blocks.text: If you searched for the master slide, you're looking for a slide layout. Apple's current Keynote guide uses that name, and the menus follow it. Apple Community replies from people on Keynote 13.1 describe the same rename, so an older guide may still say Master Slide. The idea hasn't changed. A layout is a template, and every slide built on it follows the template.
Open the layout editor in Keynote on Mac

Open the presentation you want to change. Click the View menu button in the toolbar, then choose Edit Slide Layouts. Keynote switches to layout view. Your layouts sit in the slide navigator, and the blue bar at the bottom holds the Done button you use later. You are now editing the templates, not the individual slides.

Prefer the keyboard? Press Shift-Command-E to enter layout view. Press the same keys to leave it. Apple's shortcut list gives the same combination for both directions, so you don't need a second key to get out.
Rename a layout and define its placeholders

Double-click the layout's name in the slide navigator and type a new name. Pick a name that says what the layout is for, such as Title and Photo or Quote. Names matter once a deck has several layouts, because you scan the names every time you add a slide.

A placeholder is a fixed spot that holds content. To make a text box or shape a text placeholder, select it, open the Format sidebar, click the Style tab, and choose Define as Text Placeholder. Images and video use Define as Media Placeholder in the same tab. The Display box holds the placeholder text, and the Tag box sets the tag.

items: Text placeholder: a text box or shape. Set it with Define as Text Placeholder in the Style tab.
Media placeholder: an image or video. Set it with Define as Media Placeholder in the same tab.
Object placeholder: a table, chart, or image gallery. Set it in the Format sidebar. Each layout allows only one.
Placeholder text: edit it in the Display box on the Style tab, so every slide gets the same starting wording.

blocks.text: Add, delete, and exit layouts

To add a layout, click Add Slide in the toolbar and pick a layout. You can also select a similar layout in the navigator and press Return. In layout view, Shift-Command-N adds a new layout. Start from the closest match, then change its placeholders.

To delete a layout, Control-click its thumbnail in the sidebar and choose Delete. If slides use that layout, Keynote asks you to pick a replacement. Choose the new layout in the dialog and click Choose. Then look through the slides that moved, because they now follow the replacement's design.

blocks.text: When you're done, click Done in the blue bar at the bottom. You can also choose View > Exit Slide Layouts. Changes to a layout appear on every slide based on it, so check one slide after you leave to confirm the result.
A worked example: a title slide for a lesson deck

Say you teach a unit and want every lesson to open with the same title slide. It needs a big title, a subtitle, and a photo on the right. Start in layout view and click the layout closest to that design. Rename it Lesson Title so you can find it later. Select the title box, make it a text placeholder, and check its Display text. Repeat for the subtitle. Then select the photo frame and choose Define as Media Placeholder.

Click Done. Add a slide from Lesson Title, type the lesson name into the title placeholder, and click the media placeholder to add your photo. If you later move the photo placeholder on the layout, every lesson slide built on it moves with it. You fix the layout once, and each lesson picks up the change.
Mistakes people make with slide layouts

items: Editing a slide when you meant to edit the layout. A change on one slide stays on that slide. Enter layout view for changes that should repeat.
Skipping placeholders. Content placed on a layout but not defined as a placeholder can be hard to change on each slide.
Putting two object placeholders on one layout. Each layout allows only one, so a table and a chart need separate layouts.
Deleting a layout without checking the slides. The replacement you pick changes how each affected slide looks.
Using vague names. Names like Copy are hard to find once a deck has many layouts.

blocks.title: Copy the file first
blocks.text: Layout changes apply to every slide built on a layout. Before a big restructure, copy the presentation file in Finder so you can compare the old and new versions.
Which Keynote version you have, and what it costs

Apple's Mac guide covers Keynote 15.4, but the build on your Mac may differ. Open Keynote > About Keynote to check. MacRumors reported that Keynote for Mac was updated to 14.5 on January 28, 2026, and that the free version will no longer get new features. New features go to the Creator Studio editions at version 15.1. If your menus don't match this guide, trust the menus on your Mac.

Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S., with a one-month free trial. Apple says Keynote remains free for all users, and Creator Studio adds premium content and intelligent features. Creator Studio versions of Keynote need macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later. You don't need the subscription to change a layout, and Apple's layout guide doesn't mention one.
Keynote in a browser

I could not confirm that the browser version lets you edit layouts. Apple's Keynote for iCloud guide doesn't mention master slides, slide layouts, or Edit Slide Layouts. Older third-party posts say the web version has no editable slide master, but I did not verify that. Test it on a copy before a deadline, or use the Mac app.
Where to go next

Once your layouts work, the next jobs are usually media and presenting. If your layout includes video, read [how to add a video to a slide in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/add-a-video-to-a-slide-in-keynote). For notes on your presenter view, see [how to add presenter notes in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/add-presenter-notes-in-keynote). Teachers building lesson templates can start with [Keynote for teachers on Mac](/for/teachers/keynote).

faq.question: Is the master slide still in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but Apple calls it a slide layout now. Open View > Edit Slide Layouts, or press Shift-Command-E. The idea is the same: one template that every slide built on it follows.

faq.question: Do I need Creator Studio to edit slide layouts?
faq.answer: Not as far as Apple's layout guide shows. Apple says Keynote remains free for all users. Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S., with a one-month free trial, and adds premium content and intelligent features.

faq.question: Why does my menu say Edit Slide Layout without the s?
faq.answer: Apple's guide writes both forms, and they point to the same command. Use whichever item your Mac shows. If the wording differs more, check Keynote > About Keynote for your build.

faq.question: Can one layout hold a table and a chart?
faq.answer: Not both as placeholders. Each layout allows only one Object Placeholder. Put the table on one layout and the chart on another, then pick the right layout when you add a slide.

faq.question: What happens to my slides if I delete a layout?
faq.answer: If slides use the layout you are deleting, Keynote asks you to pick a replacement. Choose the layout in the dialog and click Choose. Then look through the affected slides, since they now follow the new design.

faq.question: Do changes to a layout show on slides I already made?
faq.answer: Yes. Apple's guide says changes to a layout appear on every slide based on it. Check one slide after each change, especially if you moved a placeholder.

faq.question: Can I edit slide layouts in Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: I could not confirm it. Apple's iCloud guide does not mention slide layouts. Older third-party posts say the web version has no editable slide master, but I did not verify that for the current version. Use the Mac app to be sure.

faq.question: Can I rename a layout that slides already use?
faq.answer: Yes. Double-click its name in the slide navigator and type the new name. Your slides keep using that layout under its new name.

task: Edit a slide layout (master slide) in Keynote on Mac
appliesTo: Keynote for Mac, the slide layout editor (Apple's Mac guide covers Keynote 15.4)
requirements: Keynote for Mac installed on your Mac
A presentation open in Keynote, ideally a copy of the original
Keynote 15.4 or the build shown in Keynote > About Keynote
For Creator Studio editions, macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later

steps.name: Open the presentation
steps.text: Open the Keynote file you want to change. If the deck matters, copy the file in Finder first. Layout changes reach every slide built on that layout, so a copy gives you a safe place to test.

steps.name: Open layout view
steps.text: Click the View menu button in the toolbar, then choose Edit Slide Layouts. Keynote switches to layout view, and your layouts appear in the slide navigator. The blue bar at the bottom holds the Done button you use to leave.
steps.tip: If your menu says Edit Slide Layout without the s, it is the same command.

steps.name: Select the layout to edit
steps.text: In the slide navigator, click the layout thumbnail you want to change. Your edits apply to the layout you have selected. Scroll the navigator if the deck has many layouts.
steps.tip: Layouts and slides can look alike at small sizes. Check the name before you edit.

steps.name: Rename the layout
steps.text: Double-click the layout's name in the slide navigator. Type the new name and press Return. Pick a name that says what the layout is for, such as Title and Photo.
steps.tip: Renaming a layout does not change which layout your slides use.

steps.name: Make a text box a text placeholder
steps.text: Select the text box or shape. Open the Format sidebar, click the Style tab, and choose Define as Text Placeholder. The Display box in the Style tab holds the text that appears in that placeholder.
steps.tip: Option-Command-I shows and hides the inspector sidebars if the Format sidebar is closed.

steps.name: Make an image or video a media placeholder
steps.text: Select the image or video frame. In the Format sidebar, click the Style tab and choose Define as Media Placeholder. Every slide built on this layout now has a media spot in the same place.
steps.tip: Test the result on one slide before you build the rest.

steps.name: Set one object placeholder
steps.text: For a table, chart, or image gallery, select the object and set it as an Object Placeholder in the Format sidebar. Each layout allows only one Object Placeholder, so use a second layout for a second object.
steps.tip: Check the object's position on a slide after you leave layout view.

steps.name: Write the placeholder text and tag
steps.text: Stay in the Style tab. Type the text you want in the Display box. Use the Tag box to set the tag for that placeholder. Check how the text looks on the layout before you move on.
steps.tip: Short placeholder text tells the next person what goes in each spot.

steps.name: Add a layout
steps.text: Click Add Slide in the toolbar and pick a layout. Or select a similar layout in the navigator and press Return. In layout view, press Shift-Command-N to add a new layout.
steps.tip: Starting from a similar layout saves you from setting every placeholder again.

steps.name: Delete a layout
steps.text: Control-click the layout thumbnail in the sidebar and choose Delete. If slides use that layout, Keynote asks for a replacement. Pick the new layout in the dialog and click Choose.
steps.tip: Check the slides that moved before you finish. They take on the new layout's design.

steps.name: Leave layout view
steps.text: Click Done in the blue bar at the bottom. You can also choose View > Exit Slide Layouts, or press Shift-Command-E again.
steps.tip: Open one slide that uses the layout to confirm the change.

troubleshooting.problem: Master Slide is missing from the menus
troubleshooting.fix: Look for Edit Slide Layouts under the View menu button in the toolbar. Apple renamed the feature, and Apple Community replies from Keynote 13.1 users describe the same change. Older guides may still say Master Slide.

troubleshooting.problem: A layout change does not show on a slide
troubleshooting.fix: Check which layout the slide uses. Layout changes only reach slides built on the layout you edited. Then check the object itself. Apple's guide uses placeholders for content that should stay editable on each slide, so define those spots.

troubleshooting.problem: Placeholder font size will not change
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's guide says to choose Format > Shapes and Lines > Reset Text and Object Handles. That converts the placeholder to an eight-handled text box, which lets you change the font size by hand. Check the result on a slide, because it may no longer behave like a placeholder.

troubleshooting.problem: Delete says slides still use the layout
troubleshooting.fix: Keynote asks you to pick a replacement layout. Choose it in the dialog, click Choose, and then check the slides that used the deleted layout.

troubleshooting.problem: Menu names differ from this guide
troubleshooting.fix: Open Keynote > About Keynote to see your build. Apple's Mac guide covers Keynote 15.4. If your menu says Edit Slide Layout, use that item, since Apple's guide uses both forms.

troubleshooting.problem: Cannot find the layout editor in Keynote for iCloud
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's Keynote for iCloud guide does not cover slide layouts. Edit layouts in the Mac app, then check whether the browser version shows your changes before you rely on it.
